proposal.observation: Incumbent is still the start (proxy 0.650). Round 1 was rejected: loosening oblique Hough (27), widening both line gaps (74 and 25), raising pattern tolerance to 12, dropping curvature to 0.000366, and fitting a degree-3 centre curve cut correspondence 0.365→0.279 and broke the regular left-side assume lattice, while ring count stayed 0. Round 2 set sam.angle to 11.79 and was also rejected: all four deltas are 0.000 and the before/after images are identical, so a taper inside [7, 12] does not move this proxy. Correspondence 0.365 remains the gap (chamfer 80 px, phase incoherence 33.5°). Fill 0.752 and ring count are already healthy. Vertical bands are regular and column-bounded; the red and green fragments are short diagonals that do not stay inside those columns, and most prompt centres are assumes rather than a locked K/AB lattice.
proposal.rule: d7 already fired in the loosening direction and was rejected, so it is not repeated. d8 fires on the incumbent: prompt spacing is not a stable K/AB pattern (left assumes zigzag, centre and right rings sit on scattered slope and midpoint loci). The diagonals that are not column-bounded are the spurious-line side of that mismatch. d10 via taper does not fire as an actionable rule here, because the whole legal angle range only shifts the crop by about a centimetre and round 2 proved a null.
proposal.rationale: Keep the reference unfolding, curvature, radial gate, vertical accumulator, segment width, and angle. Those either still outscore round 1 or, for angle, cannot move the four features. Tighten the knobs round 1 loosened, and raise the horizontal vote that round 1 never touched: oblique threshold 35→50, oblique gap 60→42, horizontal gap 15→8, horizontal threshold 35→50, pattern tolerance 10→7. That asks for shorter, stronger joints and a tighter pattern so the scattered slope points are not promoted the way they were in round 1. Set sam.K_height to 1120, the block height in the only joint example that raised correspondence without a ring error, because that actually resizes the K row; do not use that example's oblique relaxation, degree-3 fit, or 7° taper. Stay clear of the tight high radial gate and the narrow segment width that collapsed fill.
